newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY - ISLES' GM MILBURY STEPS DOWN AS COACH, BOWNESS TO SUCCEED.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY - ISLES' GM MILBURY STEPS DOWN AS COACH, BOWNESS TO SUCCEED.

text.p: Mike Milbury relinquished his duties as New York Islanders head coach Friday to concentrate on his responsibilities as general manager. The move was expected.
Associate coach Rick Bowness replaced Milbury behind the bench, beginning with Thursday night's game at Hartford.

"With the upcoming draft being so important to the plan we have put in place to improve this team, I believed this is the right time and that Rick is the right guy," said Milbury, who had a 36-75-9 record in two years as Islanders coach.

The 42-year-old Bowness came to New York last season after coaching the Ottawa Senators from 1992-95. He also coached the Boston Bruins in 1991-92 and the Winnipeg Jets in 1988-89. He owns a career NHL coaching record of 83-227-33.

"It's a thrill for me," Bowness said. "We all know that this young team is on the right track and I know our players are going to get better as they mature. This is a franchise and a team that is on the upswing and that is exciting to be part of."

The Islanders are last in the Atlantic Division with a 14-23-9 record and 37 points. They have scored only 125 goals, third-lowest in the Eastern Conference, but are coming off their best performance of the season, an 8-1 rout of Edmonton on Wednesday.
New owner John Spano completed negotiations to purchase the Islanders on Wednesday, and had been discussing the coaching change with Milbury for months.

"Mike and I have been discussing this issue since last November and we discussed it again this week," said Spano. "The more we talked, the more we agreed that this is what is best for the franchise. I want that and, more than anyone, Mike wants that."
Spano's deal to buy the Islanders is expected to receive NHL approval in the coming weeks. He bought the team and its cable television rights for $165 million.
